source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: In older growing pigs, diarrhea is most often caused by internal parasites (whipworm and nodule worm, producing greenish soft faeces sometimes with blood or mucus) or swine dysentery (first appearing as soft, pale yellow-grey faeces, later with mucus and blood flecks, ranging from grey to reddish-brown, and in severe cases a porridge-like intermittent discharge). Salmonellosis is also a possible cause in this age group. Gastric ulcers can produce soft, dark faeces from stomach bleeding and may be mistaken for infectious diarrhea, so cause should not be assumed without checking other signs.
caveat: Source material on causes of diarrhea in growing pigs was only partially available this batch (the remainder of the health/disease section — main named diseases, parasite treatments, zoonoses, and post-mortem guidance — was not retrieved and is flagged as a follow-up item). This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
